pass_a_gloss: [...] freed from [every] stain. For we have been justified through faith in him, and we have been enriched with the safety from him toward anything whatever, and we have been as it were walled by the grace from him, he scaring away from us every devilish attack, and the savage risings of the opposing powers. And this he teaches, saying as to Zion, or Jerusalem, which is a Church of living God: No longer will there be added to pass through you uncircumcised and unclean. For historically you will understand the thing said in such a way: the nations dwelling around Jerusalem would be understood as uncircumcised and unclean, neither knowing God by nature and truly, nor yet having obtained the tutoring through the law; and they fought very frequently against those from the blood of Israel, so as also to be seen better in very many places than the power in them, and all but they passed through her, as having her thrown under feet. And from the things that happened historically sometimes, come, let us shape the spiritual things. The bands of the demons, that is, the world-rulers of this darkness, and with them the profane Satan, have under feet the souls not yet having come under God, and as it were go through them, no one cutting in, or defending; but when, having been made God's own, they have him as glory and strength, then indeed then the things of the greed of those will cease. For it is written that: An angel of the Lord will encamp around those who fear him, and will rescue them. So uncircumcised and unclean would be understood the loathsome and profane powers, and productive of every filth, and wicked and opposing. [Lemma, Isaiah 52:2:] Shake off the dust, and rise up, and sit, Jerusalem. Take off the bond of your neck, the captive daughter of Zion. He shows her henceforth knowing of boasts befitting saints; and in what manner she will put on the strength of her arm, and besides this the glory, he teaches clearly. First he orders to shake off the dust, and so to rise and sit, and to take off the bond of the neck; and dust in these, as I think, it is fitting to understand the earthy mind, and the uncleanness of the fleshly desires. For just as for those lying on the ground it is in every way necessary to be filled with dust and dirt, according to this same manner, I think, also for those having the mind thrown to the ground and the outlook earthy, the thoughts of fleshly uncleanness settle in. It is needed therefore that we, called into the spiritual kinship, that toward our Lord Jesus the Christ, and being about to put him on as strength and glory, shake off first the dusty and earthy mind, and cleanse first the mind, a[nd] [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: … set free from every stain. For we have been justified through faith in him, and we have been enriched with the security he gives against anything at all. We are walled about, as it were, by his grace, since he drives away from us every assault of the devil and the savage uprisings of the opposing powers.

He teaches this when he speaks to Zion, that is, to Jerusalem, which is “the Church of the living God” (1 Timothy 3:15): “The uncircumcised and unclean will no longer pass through you again” (Isaiah 52:1).

Taken historically, you will understand the saying in this way. The nations living around Jerusalem may be taken as the uncircumcised and unclean, since they neither knew the One who is God by nature and in truth nor had received the training that comes through the Law. They fought very often against those of Israel’s blood, so that in most places they were seen to be stronger than the strength Israel had, and they all but walked through Jerusalem, holding her thrown down under their feet.

Come, then, let us shape the spiritual meaning from what at times happened in history. The troops of demons, that is, “the world rulers of this darkness” (Ephesians 6:12), and with them the profane Satan, hold under their feet the souls that have not yet come under God. They pass through them, as it were, with no one to stop them, that is, no one to come to their defense. But when those souls have been made God’s own and have him as their glory and strength, then, yes then, the greed of those powers will come to an end. For it is written: “The angel of the Lord will encamp around those who fear him, and will rescue them” (Psalm 34:7).
So the uncircumcised and unclean may be understood as the loathsome and profane powers that produce every kind of filth, the wicked and opposing powers.
“Shake off the dust, and rise up, and sit down, Jerusalem. Loose the bond from your neck, captive daughter of Zion” (Isaiah 52:2).

He now shows her to be skilled in boasts fit for saints, and he teaches plainly how she will put on the strength of her arm and her glory as well (compare Isaiah 51:9; 52:1). First he commands her to shake off the dust, and so to rise and sit, and to take off the bond from her neck. Here, I think, the dust should be understood as the earthly mind and the uncleanness of fleshly desires.

For just as those who lie on the ground cannot help being covered with dust and dirt, so in the same way, I think, the thoughts of fleshly uncleanness settle on those whose mind is thrown to the ground and whose outlook is earthly. τὰς οὔπω
γεγενη- μένας ὑπὸ Θεῷ ψυχὰς
choices.english: the souls that have not yet come under God
choices.why: ὑπό with the dative: not yet under God's rule; not 'not yet begotten by God'.
rejected: souls not yet begotten by God

choices.term: ἀκά- θαρτοι νοηθεῖεν ἂν αἱ βδελυραὶ
choices.english: the uncircumcised and unclean may be understood as the loathsome and profane powers
choices.why: In the spiritual reading the unclean are the hostile powers, not powers contrary to God's strength.
God's grace as a wall against the devil's assaults.

choices.english: let us shape the spiritual meaning
choices.why: Cyril moves from the historical sense to the spiritual one.
The mind that lies on the ground gathers the dust of fleshly thoughts.
